top_story: Washington’s decision to charge an Iran-backed Iraqi militia commander with plotting attacks on Jewish sites and people across Europe and North America sharpens a threat picture that already extends beyond the Middle East and ties regional proxy networks to diaspora insecurity. The move follows months of heightened US-Iran confrontation after Trump’s March threat to destroy Iran’s power infrastructure unless Tehran reopened the Strait of Hormuz, a crisis that prompted Iranian officials to signal wider regional escalation. The separate push for the death penalty against Elias Rodriguez for killing two Israeli embassy staffers in Washington deepens the sense that violence linked to the Israeli-Iranian confrontation is bleeding into Western civic space and Jewish communal life. The emerging pattern is a more diffuse conflict in which state pressure, militia activity, and lone-actor violence reinforce each other and raise the risk of retaliatory cycles far from the Gulf.
